channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro não disse que privatizará SUS se for eleito presidente
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro did not say he would privatize the SUS if elected president, as verified by UOL Confere. The claims circulating on social media are false and distort a CNN Brasil column on health proposals. The senator's press office labeled the posts as 'a gross fabrication full of lies'.

item.title: Justiça nega remoção de vídeo em que Janones chama Bolsonaro de 'vagabundo' e 'ladrão'
item.description: The District Federal Court of Justice (TJDFT) denied Jair Bolsonaro's urgent request to remove a video in which federal deputy André Janones calls him a 'vagabond', 'thief', and 'bastard'. The ruling upholds freedom of expression, even amid personal attacks between public figures. The case highlights the ongoing tension between honor and free speech in Brazil's political environment.

item.title: Fazenda diz buscar estabilidade da dívida; estoque subiu R$ 3 tri
item.description: Brazil's gross debt increased by R$ 2.95 trillion under President Lula, raising the debt-to-GDP ratio from 71.7% to 79.2%. The National Treasury reports the Federal Public Debt (DPF) stock rose from R$ 5.95 trillion to R$ 8.84 trillion between December 2025 and February 2026. The Ministry of Finance states it has a consistent medium- and long-term plan to reduce public debt, to be detailed in the 2027 Budget Guidelines Law (PLDO), and attributes discrepancies with IMF projections to methodological differences, particularly in how Central Bank-held securities are treated.

item.title: TSE apresenta diagnóstico inédito sobre a representatividade racial no sistema eleitoral
item.description: The TSE unveiled an unprecedented diagnosis showing that, despite increased racial self-declaration in elections, Black representation in political power still does not reflect Brazil’s societal composition. Based on data from 2014 to 2024, the study reveals that invisible party filtering mechanisms limit the impact of public campaign funding (FEFC) aimed at Black candidacies, even with affirmative action policies in place. TSE President Minister Cármen Lúcia stressed that the current challenge is ensuring public resources not only reach Black candidates but are used under real competitive conditions.

item.title: Haddad diz que o PT está “cercando as bets há algum tempo”
item.description: Fernando Haddad, the PT's pre-candidate for governor of São Paulo, said the party has been 'surrounding the bets for some time', describing sports betting as a public health issue. He noted that people are already being treated by the Ministry of Health due to gambling. PT congressional leader Pedro Uczai filed Bill 1.808/2026, which bans fixed-odds betting nationwide and repeals the 2018 and 2023 laws that established the legal framework for sports betting and online gaming, aligning with President Lula’s stance that betting companies should be shut down if they cause harm.

item.title: Moraes rejeita autorização para irmão de Michelle ser cuidador de Bolsonaro
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes denied a request by Jair Bolsonaro's legal team to allow permanent visitation rights for Carlos Eduardo Antunes Torres, the foster brother of former first lady Michelle Bolsonaro. The defense had sought to have Torres recognized as Bolsonaro's caregiver. The ruling was issued on Wednesday, April 15.

item.title: Flávio fala em “cerco jurídico” após inquérito autorizado por Moraes
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), a pre-candidate for president, denounced a 'legal siege' after Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes authorized an inquiry into alleged slander against President Lula. The investigation stems from a post Bolsonaro made on X on January 3, in which he allegedly falsely attributed statements or actions to the president. The case heightens the political clash between the Bolsonaro clan and the Lula government.

item.title: Gilmar suspende julgamento sobre nomeação de parentes em cargos políticos
item.description: Justice Gilmar Mendes requested a view and suspended the STF's judgment on whether appointing relatives to political offices constitutes nepotism, with the prior vote at 6-1 in favor of the view that it does not fall under Binding Precedent 13. The rapporteur Luiz Fux changed his vote to apply the ban, with a modulation allowing exception if qualified third parties declined the appointment, joined by Flávio Dino and Cármen Lúcia, while Dino and Cármen Lúcia maintained their original vote against any exception. The case may remain suspended for up to 90 days due to the view request.

item.title: Lula dá sinais de que pode rever indicação de Otto Lobo para presidir CVM
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has signaled to allies that he may reconsider the nomination of Otto Lobo to preside over the CVM (Securities and Exchange Commission), following a conversation with Senator Eduardo Braga (MDB-AM), who was chosen as the rapporteur for the nomination. The potential reversal reflects political maneuvering surrounding the appointment to the capital markets regulator.

item.title: CPIs que miraram Lulinha e STF foram desperdício do seu dinheiro, eleitores
item.description: The CPIs targeting President Lula's son and the Supreme Court were characterized as electoral spectacles, with predictable outcomes and little impact on real issues such as pensioner theft and criminal faction violence. Congress allegedly used public funds for political theater rather than addressing urgent public demands.

item.title: Governo deve incluir cerca de 40% das sentenças judiciais no cálculo da meta fiscal de 2027
item.description: The Lula government plans to include approximately 40% of total judicial sentencing expenses in the 2027 fiscal target, according to economic team sources consulted by Folha. The measure aims to broaden the scope of fiscal adjustment, reflecting the growing impact of judicial decisions on the public budget. Including these expenses would be an effort to increase transparency and accountability in public finances.

item.title: Menos trabalho, mais crescimento? O impasse do fim da escala 6×1
item.description: President Lula’s proposal to reduce the workweek from 6x1 to 5x2, with a maximum of 40 hours and no salary cut, has sparked debate over economic impacts. While Deputy Érika Hilton’s PEC proposes a 36-hour workweek, the Executive’s bill sets 40 hours, seen as more palatable by the opposition since it does not amend the Constitution. Economists warn the measure could raise labor costs in a low-unemployment context, with simulations suggesting a potential 2.6% GDP drop under 40 hours and up to 7.4% under 36 hours — equivalent to losing two years of robust growth.

item.title: Haddad diz que recusou receber Vorcaro várias vezes
item.description: Haddad said he repeatedly refused to meet with banker Daniel Vorcaro, owner of Banco Master, after being warned by his Finance Ministry team about irregularities in the bank's accounts, which he likened to 'nitroglycerin'. Despite this, Poder360 reported that Lula met with Vorcaro in December 2024, discussing banking concentration, even after alerts. The meeting included several ministers and executives, and the Central Bank, under Galípolo, later rejected the sale of Master to BRB and liquidated the institution due to R$12 billion in frauds.

item.title: Crusoé: “O intocável ataca novamente”, diz Zema sobre Gilmar
item.description: Romeu Zema, pre-candidate for President from the Novo party, responded to criticisms from Supreme Court Minister Gilmar Mendes, who publicly objected to Zema's remarks regarding STF decisions favorable to Minas Gerais during his governorship. Zema characterized Mendes' reaction as another attack from the 'untouchable,' implying the minister is beyond criticism. The exchange reflects growing tensions between the Executive and Judiciary, with Zema defending his comments as legitimate institutional critique.

item.title: Governistas projetam pelo menos 48 votos no Senado para aprovar Jorge Messias
item.description: Lula's government allies project at least 48 votes in the Senate to approve Jorge Messias's nomination to the STF, relying on a 'silent vote' from senators who do not declare support publicly but signal backing in private. The CCJ hearing is scheduled for April 28, with expectations of approval by simple majority, and rapporteur Weverton Rocha has already issued a favorable opinion.

item.title: Aportes para MCMV são ampliados para R$ 200 bilhões
item.description: The federal government increased funding for the Minha Casa, Minha Vida (MCMV) program by R$ 20 billion, bringing the total to a record R$ 200 billion. President Lula announced that the program has already contracted 2 million homes ahead of schedule and aims to reach 3 million by year-end, emphasizing housing as a human right and the FGTS as a key tool for boosting the construction sector and national economic growth.

item.title: Vídeo: CCJ do Senado marca para dia 28 sabatina de Jorge Messias, indicado ao STF
item.description: The Senate's Constitution and Justice Committee (CCJ) moved up the confirmation hearing for Jorge Messias, nominated to the Supreme Federal Court (STF), from April 29 to April 28. The favorable opinion, presented by Senator Weverton (PDT-MA), was read on April 15. Messias, current Attorney General of the Union, needs at least 41 favorable votes for approval in the plenary session on the same day as the hearing.

item.title: Veja fotos da Marcha da Classe Trabalhadora em Brasília
item.description: The Workers' Class March took place in Brasília on April 15, 2026, organized by trade union centrals including the CUT, with demands focused on ending the 6x1 work schedule, regulating app-based workers, and ensuring collective bargaining rights for public servants. CUT President Sérgio Nobre stated that the Lula government had submitted a proposal to Congress to reduce the 6x1 schedule and announced that union leaders would declare support for Lula's re-election after meeting with him. The march concluded with planned meetings with Chamber President Hugo Motta and President Lula to deliver the 2026/2030 workers' agenda.

item.title: Centrais sindicais promovem marcha em Brasília pelo fim da escala 6 X 1
item.description: On April 15, 2026, trade unions held the Workers' Class March in Brasília, demanding the end of the 6×1 work schedule, regulation of app-based work, and negotiation rights for public servants. CUT president Sérgio Nobre said workers are pleased with the government's submission of a 6×1 reduction proposal to Congress and that leaders should thank the president and declare support for his re-election campaign.

item.title: Governo Tarcísio questiona ineditismo anunciado por gestão Lula sobre tecnologia assistiva
item.description: The São Paulo state government, led by Tarcísio de Freitas, questioned the novelty of an announcement by the federal Lula administration regarding the creation of a research center in assistive technology for people with disabilities, stating that such initiatives already existed before and expressing 'strangeness' at the claim of pioneering.

item.title: Presidente da CPMI do INSS entrega relatório final a Fux e Mendonça
item.description: The president of the INSS CPI, Carlos Viana (PSD-MG), will deliver the final report of the commission to Supreme Court Ministers Luiz Fux and André Mendonça on Wednesday, April 15, 2026, at 4:00 PM. The report, rejected by a vote of 19 to 12, called for the indictment of 216 individuals, including President Lula’s eldest son, Fábio Luís Lula da Silva (Lulinha), and two former Social Security ministers, on charges such as corruption, money laundering, and organized crime.

item.title: Com caneta de 1989, Lula assina obras do PAC e titula quilombolas
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva signed service orders for Novo PAC infrastructure projects in Sergipe and decrees for the titulation of quilombola territories, using a symbolic pen from his 1989 presidential campaign. He stressed the need for immediate and concrete impacts on people's lives, linking investments to locally proposed projects with clear start and end points. Lula also demanded a focus on tangible deliveries amid political narrative disputes.

item.title: Escala 6x1: entenda principais pontos e diferenças entre textos do Congresso e do governo
item.description: Relator Paulo Azi (União-BA) issued a favorable report on PECs to end the 6x1 work scale, but an opposition request for view delayed voting in the CCJ by up to 15 days. Three proposals are under consideration: Erika Hilton’s PEC (4-day week in 360 days), Reginaldo Lopes’ PEC (36-hour week in 10 years), and the Lula government’s PL with constitutional urgency. The debate centers on tensions between reducing work hours and impacts on competitiveness and job creation, with calls for productivity gains via worker training, innovation, and infrastructure investment.

item.title: Bolsonaro hijo, investigado por calumnias a Lula en un mensaje sobre el presidente brasileño, Maduro y el narcotráfico
item.description: Brazilian Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, is under investigation for defamation after linking President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva to drug trafficking, money laundering, and support for terrorists in a post on X (formerly Twitter). The post followed a false report of Nicolás Maduro’s capture by U.S. forces on January 3, and included images of Maduro allegedly arrested and a fabricated headline claiming Lula had called an emergency meeting. The allegations are part of a broader narrative tying Lula to the 'São Paulo Forum' and illicit activities.

item.title: Análise: avanço de Flávio entre homens, jovens e classe média explica empate com Lula, diz Quaest
item.description: The technical tie between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro in voting intentions for the 2026 presidential runoff is explained by the senator’s gains among men, youth, and the middle class, according to Quaest analysis. While Lula retains advantages among women, low-income voters, and those over 60, Flávio is consolidating support in key demographics, particularly among earners of 2 to 5 minimum wages — where the government expected impact from income tax exemption. Although still within the margin of error, this marks the first time Flávio numerically leads Lula in the poll.

item.title: Flávio diz que Lula usa “coleguinhas” para intimidar, mas não conseguirá
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) claimed that President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) could use his 'little friends' in government to intimidate him, but would fail, insisting Lula will not be president after 2027. The statement came after Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes opened an inquiry into the senator for defamation, based on a January 2026 post linking Lula to Venezuelan Nicolás Maduro and alleging drug trafficking, money laundering, and election fraud. Flávio called the investigation 'juridically fragile' and an attack on free speech and parliamentary mandate.

item.title: As intenções de voto de Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro entre católicos e evangélicos, segundo a Quaest
item.description: Lula leads voting intentions in the first turn among Catholic voters at 43%, while Flávio Bolsonaro leads among evangelicals at 43%. Overall, Lula has 37% and Flávio 32% in the first round, but in the second-round projection, Flávio is numerically ahead at 42% versus Lula’s 40%, within a technical tie.

item.title: Pedido de vista adia votação da PEC do fim da 6x1 na CCJ da Câmara
item.description: A collective request for vista by PSDB and PL postponed the vote on PEC 221/2019 in the CCJ, which aims to end the 6x1 work schedule and reduce the weekly workload to 36 hours over ten years. Despite the rapporteur Paulo Azi (União-BA) issuing a favorable opinion on the constitutionality of the reduction, the vote was delayed for further analysis. President Lula sent a constitutionally urgent bill to abolish the 6x1 scale and reduce the workweek to 40 hours, with a 45-day voting deadline, creating tension with the PEC’s legislative process.

item.title: STF endurece discurso e pode reagir à atuação das CPIs, avaliam analistas
item.description: The rejection of the Organized Crime CPI report, which sought the indictment of STF ministers, sparked tensions between the Judiciary and Congress, with ministers Dino, Mendes, and Toffoli condemning the initiative as politically motivated and potentially abusive. Toffoli suggested such actions could lead to the ineligibility of lawmakers for attacking institutions with electoral aims, though analysts view this as remote. Experts noted the CPI deviated from its original purpose and that the STF may respond by setting limits on future CPI powers.

item.title: Áudio: CCJ aprova indicados ao CNJ e CNMP
item.description: The Senate's Constitution and Justice Committee (CCJ) approved seven nominations for the National Council of Justice (CNJ) and the National Council of the Public Ministry (CNMP), referenced as OFS 16/2025 through OFS 3/2026. The nominations will now proceed to a vote in the Senate Plenary. In the same meeting, Senator Weverton (PDT-MA) presented the report on the nomination of Jorge Messias, Attorney General of the Union, for a seat on the Supreme Federal Court, with his confirmation hearing before the CCJ scheduled for April 29.

item.title: A nova data para a sabatina de Jorge Messias no Senado
item.description: The sabatina for Jorge Messias, Lula's nominee to the Supreme Federal Court, has been moved up to April 28, Tuesday, at the request of rapporteur Weverton Rocha, due to the proximity of the May 1st holiday. After the hearing, Messias must still be approved by the Constitution and Justice Committee and the Senate plenary, where he needs at least 41 secret votes.

item.title: Moraes indica defensor público para defesa de Tagliaferro e marca nova audięncia
item.description: Justice Alexandre de Moraes has ordered the Federal Public Defender's Office to represent Eduardo Tagliaferro, his former aide at the TSE, and scheduled a new hearing in the case.

item.title: PF prende dono da Choquei, MC Ryan e Poze do Rodo em operaçăo contra lavagem de dinheiro
item.description: Federal Police arrested the owner of Choquei, MC Ryan, and MC Poze do Rodo in a money laundering operation. The arrests occurred the same day as a Genial/Quaest poll showed Lula leading alone in the first round of the 2026 elections, with Flávio having a numerical advantage in the second round, according to analysis by Josias de Souza and Leonardo Sakamoto. Additional highlights include app drivers protesting against PLP 152 in São Paulo and NASA releasing new details about the Artemis II astronaut rescue.

item.title: Lula lidera no 1ş turno e Flávio tem vantagem numérica no 2ş, diz Quaest; Josias e Sakamoto analisam
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll released on April 15, 2026 shows President Lula (PT) leading in isolated first-round voting intentions for the 2026 elections. In a potential runoff, Flávio Dino holds a numerical advantage over his likely opponent. Columnists Josias de Souza and Leonardo Sakamoto analyze the results, highlighting the current political landscape.

item.title: Senador petista é hospitalizado e passará por cirurgia no quadril
item.description: Senator Paulo Paim (PT-RS) was hospitalized at Sírio-Libanês Hospital after tests indicated the need for hip surgery. He had previously disclosed health issues last year when deciding not to run for Senate re-election. Paim reaffirmed his commitment to support, as much as possible, the PT’s electoral project in Rio Grande do Sul and President Lula’s re-election campaign.

item.title: Decisão de Moraes contra Flávio pode fortalecer uma narrativa na guerra eleitoral
item.description: Justice Alexandre de Moraes' decision to authorize an investigation against Senator Flávio Bolsonaro for alleged defamation of President Lula has reignited the debate over the boundaries between free speech and criminal liability, after Bolsonaro accused Lula of drug trafficking and money laundering without evidence. While political criticism is part of democratic discourse, analysts argue that unsubstantiated serious accusations may cross the line into slander, and the probe could shape electoral narratives—bolstering a persecution narrative among his base while potentially harming his appeal among broader voters.

item.title: Escala 6×1: presidente da CCJ da Câmara concede vista das PECs e votação é adiada
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies' Constitution and Justice Committee (CCJ) postponed the vote on the favorable report regarding two PECs proposing to end the 6×1 work scale, after a request for more time by Deputy Lucas Redecker, who cited the topic's sensitivity. The PECs, one by Reginaldo Lopes (PT-MG) and another by Erika Hilton (PSOL-SP), set a daily limit of 8 hours and weekly limit of 36 hours, differing in weekly work schedule and effective date. Reporter Paulo Azi (União Brasil-BA) assessed only constitutional admissibility, not substance, and emphasized the need for discussion on transition rules, Social Security impact, and employer compensation.

item.title: Moraes nega visita de irmão de Michelle para cuidar de Bolsonaro
item.description: Minister Alexandre de Moraes denied the defense's request to allow permanent visitation by Michelle Bolsonaro's brother to Jair Bolsonaro's residence under humanitarian house arrest. The ruling states that only healthcare, security professionals, and previously authorized individuals may enter, rejecting family or domestic reasons as valid grounds. Moraes emphasized there is no technical justification for the exception, as the individual is not a healthcare professional.

item.title: Pesquisa Quaest: velocidade de Flávio e votos soltos embaralham disputa com Lula
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll reveals a polarized race between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, with the senator gaining rapid momentum as the consolidated figure of Bolsonarism. Although Lula still leads, his advantage has narrowed, and the second round shows a technical tie. The significant share of undecided or blank/null voters remains a key factor that could determine the outcome.

item.title: Flávio diz que inquérito de Moraes sobre Lula tenta “cercear liberdade”
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) criticized Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes' decision to authorize an investigation against him for alleged slander against President Lula, calling it legally weak and an attempt to restrict freedom of speech. He argued his January 2026 post, which linked Lula to Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and mentioned potential whistleblowing, merely reported publicly known facts about Maduro's imprisonment without directly accusing Lula of crimes. Flávio compared the move to what he described as electoral imbalance by the TSE in 2022 and affirmed his constitutional duty to oversee the government.

item.title: Nomes de indicados ao CNMP são aprovados na CCJ e vão a Plenário
item.description: The Constitution and Justice Committee (CCJ) unanimously approved the nominations of Márcio Barra Lima and Carl Olav Smith for the National Council of the Public Ministry (CNMP). The candidates were questioned on public safety and investigative powers, receiving 22 votes in favor. The nominations will be voted on in the Plenary later this Wednesday.

item.title: Aliados de Flávio Bolsonaro avaliam que entrada de Caiado na eleição leva disputa ao 2º turno
item.description: Allies of Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) believe that Ronaldo Caiado's (PSD) entry into the 2026 presidential race will guarantee a runoff, which they view as positive for the opposition campaign. They see Caiado's candidacy as fragmenting the government-aligned bloc and increasing the opposition's chances of victory.

item.title: Deputado aciona TJ para que Alerj não realize eleição interna até decisão do STF
item.description: State Deputy Luiz Paulo (PSD) filed a writ of security with the TJ of Rio to prevent Alerj from convening internal elections for the presidency of the House until the STF decides on the format of the supplementary election for the state government. The action aims to avoid internal proceedings before the judicial definition of the state election. The article is subscriber-only.

item.title: Lula sai em defesa de Papa em mensagem à Igreja Católica após ataques de Trump
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva issued a message defending Pope Leo XV after criticism from Donald Trump, who claimed credit for the pope’s election and accused him of being too political. Lula stated that defenders of peace have been attacked by powerful figures who see themselves as deities, emphasizing that love for one’s neighbor outweighs the power of weapons and money. He also referenced the National Conference of Bishops of Brazil (CNBB) and its role in defending democracy and opposing the military dictatorship.

item.title: STF AO VIVO – Nepotismo em cargos políticos e quebra ampla de sigilo – sessão de 15/4/2026
item.description: The STF resumes the hearing of two extraordinary appeals: RE 1.133.118, examining whether the anti-nepotism rule applies to political offices such as municipal or state secretary and federal minister; and RE 1177984, concerning whether the state must inform suspects of their right to silence during police approach or only during formal interrogation. Also on the agenda are RE 1301250, challenging judicial authorization for breaking internet search history secrecy without defined suspects (linked to the Marielle Franco case), and the joint judgment of ADPF 342 and ACO 2463, assessing the constitutionality of Law 5.709/71 restricting rural land purchases by Brazilian companies with foreign capital.

item.title: Gilmar Mendes avalia acionar PGR contra Alessandro Vieira
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Gilmar Mendes is considering filing a criminal complaint against Senator Alessandro Vieira (MDB-SE) for alleged abuse of authority, after Vieira requested the indictment of STF ministers and the Attorney General in the Organized Crime CPI, a request rejected by the committee. Mendes argues the report overstepped the CPI’s authority by attempting to initiate impeachment proceedings against justices, characterizing it as an electoral move and an attack on democratic institutions.

item.title: Em mensagem a católicos, Lula manifesta solidariedade ao papa Leão XIV em episódio envolvendo Trump
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva expressed solidarity with Pope Leo XIV, stating that defenders of peace are often attacked by powerful figures who see themselves as divine. The remarks came amid criticism from U.S. President Donald Trump, who called the pope 'weak' and 'terrible in foreign policy' for advocating diplomatic solutions to international conflicts.

item.title: Reforma Casa Brasil: governo amplia crédito para reforma de moradias para quem tem renda até R$ 13 mil
item.description: The federal government expanded the Reforma Casa Brasil program, raising the maximum family income eligible for credit from R$9,600 to R$13,000, increasing the maximum loan amount from R$30,000 to R$50,000, cutting interest rates to 0.99% per month for all income brackets, and extending the repayment term from 60 to 72 months. The FGHab will now guarantee all loans, with Caixa Econômica Federal as the operator. Announced in an election year, the initiative targets Brazil’s structural housing deficit by financing renovations of existing homes, not just new construction.

item.title: Janja vai à Espanha antes de Lula para agenda sobre feminicídio
item.description: First Lady Janja Lula da Silva advanced her trip to Spain to attend an agenda focused on combating femicide, including a visit to the VioGén system, meetings with equality authorities, and a stop at the Centro Cometa in Madrid. The itinerary reinforces her role as a public policy articulator on women's rights, a government priority in an election year, given that 53% of Brazil's electorate is female.

item.title: Agência de comunicação vence licitação em SP e atenderá governos Lula e Tarcísio
item.description: Communication agency Calia Y2 controlled by FSB won bidding to serve São Paulo government and Presidency with a R$ 300 million per year contract.
